selection: Purposeful fixed existing tracks across three sources, including known detector failures; not an unbiased population sample.
primary: Captured-correct to restored-wrong majority speaking answer, repeated in both runs.
expansion_gate: Proceed to larger restoration-induced Qwen majority-error study only if repeated primary harm occurs on at least two distinct source videos.
secondary: Wrong timestamp tags and abstention coverage; never substitute for primary gate.
scope: Qwen tool-agent using cached real FastDVDnet/TalkNet measurements, not direct video perception. Synthetic Gaussian noise, dataset annotations.
interface_change: Explicit audio-only scope; uniform audio-visual and audio-only heads, no visual-only head. Fixed for every case and condition.
system_prompt: You are a tool-using audiovisual assistant deciding whether one visible person is speaking. You cannot see or hear media directly. Inspect current evidence before answering. The audio-visual detector estimates whether THIS visible person speaks. The audio-only head measures activity in the audio and CANNOT identify the visible speaker: another person or offscreen person may be speaking. Neither head is ground truth; scores are uncalibrated. Image-quality scores measure appearance, not speaker correctness. You may disagree with the detector. Do not invent identities, words, visual observations, or ground truth. Give a best binary majority-speaking answer and separate timestamped tags, using -1 for uncertain timestamps. Confidence is self-reported, not calibrated. Submit through submit_answer within six model calls.
user_prompt: For this one-second clip, is the visible person speaking for the majority of the 24 scored timestamps? Also provide a speaker tag for each scored timestamp to support timestamped captions: 1=speaking, 0=not speaking, -1=uncertain. Explain your evidence briefly. Do not attribute words to anyone.
